x.summary: Peter Yang 近期分享了多个高价值 AI 实用指南与行业见解：首先，他提供了一套精细化提示词（Prompt），用于审计并清理与 Google 账号绑定的数十个 AI 应用和 Agent 权限；其次，他高度评价了 Claude Code 的性能进化，称其速度和易用性已超越 ChatGPT，但仍期待补齐 Computer Use 和实时语音功能；此外，他还探讨了利用 AI 加速游戏开发以及“以实战交付取代传统面试”的高效招聘模式。
x.translation:
【关于招聘体系】
应将“实战试用”（Work trials）作为招聘的常态，而非传统面试。来自 @APompliano 的分享：“我们当时想开发一个特定功能，就直接对候选人说：‘嘿，给你两周时间把它做出来。’期间他问了一些问题、熟悉了环境，但他真的做出来了。老兄，我根本不需要质疑你能不能胜任这里的工作，我们没有浪费四周时间走到这一步，而是直接上线了一个新功能。”

【关于 AI 工具评估】
必须为 @amorriscode 及其团队点赞——Claude Code 应用现在运行速度飞快，可以说比 ChatGPT 更加简单易用。目前唯一尚缺的是更强的浏览器/电脑操作（Computer Use）、针对所有线程的远程控制以及实时语音功能。

【关于安全与 Agent 审计 Prompt】
如果你和我一样，Google 账号绑定了太多应用和 Agent（整整 45 个！），这里有一个用于审计和清理的提示词：
“请帮我审计我的 Google 应用连接（https://myaccount.google.com/connections）：
1. 审查所有连接类别中的每一个应用。主动询问我还在使用哪些，而不是主观猜测。
2. 打开每个应用的详情。区分基础 Google 登录与访问 Gmail、Drive、日历或其他数据的权限。
3. 给出保留、断开连接或询问我的建议。解释你的推理以及可能停止工作的服务。标记出过宽的权限、不熟悉的提供商和重复条目。
4. 在更改任何内容前展示你的建议。仅断开我明确批准的应用，并核实已移除。不要删除应用账号或取消订阅。”

【关于游戏开发】
Tim 说的太对了。希望开发《星际争霸 3》的开发者能看到这条推文，积极拥抱 AI，在 2030 年前将游戏发售。
x.recommendation: Peter Yang 的分享兼具强实用性与前瞻视角。无论是一键审计 Agent 权限的高效 Prompt，还是对 Claude Code 工具链发展的精准点评，亦或是用交付成果替代传统面试的敏捷思想，都能为 AI 开发者、产品经理及团队管理者带来即学即用的生产力启发。

x.summary: Anthropic Claude Code 团队开发者 Thariq 探讨了 AI 时代游戏体验的深刻变革。他发现相比于亲自玩《英雄联盟》等高脑力消耗的游戏，使用 AI 进行“氛围编码”（Vibe Coding）来开发游戏片段反而带来更大的乐趣。基于此，他提出了一项开源游戏设想：将“用 AI 创作角色与机制”作为游戏的核心玩法，由系统自动平衡数值，从而让“创作过程”本身成为全新的游戏娱乐形态。
x.translation:
[推文 1] 我最近意识到，如今我往往更喜欢通过“氛围编码”（Vibe Code）来制作游戏的小部件，而不是真正去玩游戏。尤其是像《英雄联盟》这样需要深度思考的游戏。我不太确定这对于未来的游戏行业究竟意味着什么，但我认为这非常重要。

[推文 2] 这里的游戏机制会是什么样的？你的角色会自动战斗吗，就像 Salty Bet 那样？还是说在战斗中会有很酷的电影级选择，就像《女神异闻录》（Persona）或《暴雨》（Heavy Rain）那样？我还不确定！等我想明白了会分享更多。

[推文 3] 我脑海里反复出现的一个卖点是：在制作游戏和角色时获得的乐趣，和玩游戏本身一样多。如果把这个作为最大的卖点会怎样？我会将这个游戏开源发布，你可以 Vibe Code 属于你自己的角色，而系统会自动对角色进行数值平衡。
x.recommendation: 来自 Anthropic 核心 Builder 对“AI 驱动的互动娱乐”的前沿思考。随着 AI 编程门槛的大幅降低，“玩家”与“开发者”的身份界限正在模糊，Vibe Coding 正在成为一种新型的玩法体验，对游戏设计与 Generative AI 落地产品有极高的启示意义。

x.author: Aaron Levie
x.role: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
x.summary: Aaron Levie 近期分享了关于技术与产品的最新动态，重点涉及技术路线、产品进展与一线实践思考。
x.translation:
Here’s why agent swarms are going to be a very big deal. We can finally make compute a critical variable in a large number of important tasks in the economy which wasn’t possible before.

There’s a large amount of work in the world that is essentially only constrained by the amount of time that we put into research, data processing, discovery work, running tests, and more. All of this work is bottlenecked by our ability to plan, execute, review, and coordinate everything happening in these workflows. Which means we basically do very little of them today relative to their economic value. 

Agent swarms are the first real ability to parallelize this work in a way where - in theory - the only parameter that matters is how much compute you throw at the problem. Cyber security, life sciences or material science research, trading, QA testing, data processing, and many other fields are essentially compute constrained problems in the limit once models are good enough at these tasks.

The breakthrough is that in a world where agents can use tools, write code, process data, have strong domain depth, and can coordinate with each other, you can begin to solve arbitrarily complex problems by setting the right goals and applying enough tokens to the problem. This changes a lot of fields as well as even the competitive dynamics in these fields.

The biggest misread of anyone predicting the end of software engineering was imagining that the world only needed a certain amount of software, and bringing automation to the field would reduce the need for labor. 

Exactly the opposite is happening where essentially most things are actually turning into software. Because agents can use tools, work with computers, write software on the fly, and process data like humans (but far faster), we can now throw “software” at problems that never could reasonably be digitized before.

What that leads to is the role of engineering taking on greater importance in the economy, because we can now engineer far more systems and processes than were possible before.

If you’re a bank trying to do new forms of trading, engineers are often your first bet. If you are in life sciences, you expect more and more research and lab work to be engineering centric. If you’re in manufacturing, you’re trying to automate more of the supply chain, all that is engineering. More and more work is shaped like software problems.

Yes we’re not going to be coding manually in the future. But almost everything will be code, which means those that understand it are in a fantastic position.

It’s incredible to have reached a threshold where it’s practical that AI will be better at training models than humans are so quickly. One day recursive self improvement feels far off, and the next we already have signs of what it will look like.

Model capability finally exceeding most human engineers, advancements in the harness and infra for long running agents, a growing array of data, and the ability to parallelize the agents to work on vastly more tasks and tests and approaches than any person could have before, creates an incredible flywheel. 

This flywheel will almost certainly accelerate model progress far faster than we’ve seen before - or at a minimum enable pushing up the ceiling of the frontier at an insane rate. If you aren’t pricing in what RSI will lead to, that’s probably a mistake.

So in fact we actually can get robots, flying cars, superintelligence, fast internet on planes, space travel, space colonies, orbital data centers, unlimited energy, likely cures for nearly every disease, and more all in our life times. Pretty great. https://t.co/jhgqv8gXhb

They did it. They made a Muse open weights model, which is a huge step forward for OSS in the US. 

This is going to further accelerate AI diffusion because enterprises will be able to mix and match frontier performance for orchestration and high end tasks, while being able to have low cost and tailored post trained models for repeatable workflows. 

Overall this dramatically increases token consumption and workloads across the stack. Great to see Meta doing this.

Moving from chatting back and forth with agents, to having agents that you spin up in the background to do useful work for you is probably on the order of 100X or 1000X more token consumption than what we’re seeing today. 

Most work right now is essentially rate limited by our ability to process and work with information. Moving data between systems. Reviewing a document. Looking through code for security issues. Processing log data to look for even patterns. Looking up information about a prospective client. Almost all of knowledge work is constrained by these steps, and AI has become a huge unlock to that. 

So our first step was to use AI to do these individual tasks much faster for us. That was the chatbot phenomenon that we have been experiencing for the past 3+ years. But we can still then only augment the work that we remain in the loop for, and we’re highly limited by our ability to parallelize this work by our own bandwidth and context.

But where we’re going is quite different. As AI models continue to improve at incredible rates, we can hand off more and more work to the agent. First it’s letting the agent run with a harder problem. Then it’s giving a few agents multiple parts of a task at once. But we’re not far off from being able to throw an arbitrary number of agents at a problem and just say “come back when you’ve accomplished this goal”. 

Now imagine that agent swarm for any problem we can think of. Protecting our codebases, data, and systems. blogs.title: How we contain Claude across products
blogs.summary: Anthropic 在本文中探讨了如何通过“限制爆炸半径（Blast Radius）”来安全部署 Claude 智能体。核心观点认为，随着模型能力增强，单纯依赖“人在回路（Human-in-the-loop）”的监督模式因用户疲劳（93%的批准率）而失效，必须转向“容器化与环境隔离”的防御策略。Anthropic 分享了在 claude.ai、Claude Code 和 Claude Cowork 三款产品中，通过沙箱、虚拟机及出口控制等手段实现权限边界管理的工程经验，强调了在提升智能体效能与控制潜在风险之间寻找平衡的重要性。
blogs.translation: 一年前，我们绝不会允许 Claude 拥有可能导致内部服务瘫痪的权限，但现在这已成为常态。部署智能体的风险由“故障概率”和“潜在损害（爆炸半径）”组成。随着模型能力提升，我们无法完全消除风险，因此工程重点转向了如何通过环境控制来限制爆炸半径。我们发现，依赖人类逐次确认的监督模式存在“批准疲劳”，用户往往会机械性地点击通过。因此，我们转向了更稳健的“容器化防御”，通过沙箱、虚拟机和出口流量控制来严格限制智能体的操作边界，并针对不同产品形态构建了差异化的安全架构。
blogs.recommendation: 该文为企业级 AI 应用提供了极具价值的工程实践参考，特别是关于如何通过环境隔离（而非仅依赖模型对齐）来降低智能体失控风险的思路。对于正在开发 Agent 产品或涉及自动化工作流的团队，文中关于“批准疲劳”的观察及多层级容器化防御架构具有直接的落地借鉴意义。

podcasts.summary:
【核心 Takeaway】数据库正在从 AI 的“向量检索备忘录”演进为智能体（AI Agents）进行高频读写与自动治理的主战场。
【反直觉洞见】大多数人对“AI+数据库”的认知仍停留在两年前的向量检索（RAG）阶段，但如今 AI Agents 正在以惊人速度直接创建、写入甚至删除生产数据库。忽视传统数据库的事务与安全约束，盲目让 Agent 接管生产库极易引发灾难。
【精彩金句】不懂数据库历史就盲目搞 Agent 开发，“就像给一只猎豹喂满了可卡因，再把它塞进一辆法拉利里。”
podcasts.translation:
1. **Agent 时代的数据库危机**：AI 智能体正快速学会直接操作数据库，但由于开发者缺乏对传统数据库历史与原理的敬畏，导致生产数据库被 Agent 误删的事故屡见不鲜。
2. **从 RAG 演进至 Agent 交互**：两年前“AI+数据库”的核心是向量数据库与近似最近邻搜索（ANN），用于处理模糊语义查询；而今天，数据库迎来了 Agent 自动建表、写库与复杂管理的新纪元。
3. **顶尖学者的行业洞察**：CMU 数据库领域的“神级”教授 Andy Pavlo 宣布加入 ClickHouse 并创立 ClickHouse Labs，本期节目深入探讨了在 AI Agents 狂飙的当下，底层数据库架构应如何应对与演进。
podcasts.recommendation: 本期节目由 CMU 数据库顶尖学者 Andy Pavlo 倾情献声，用极具幽默感的语言破译了 AI Agents 狂飙背后的数据库安全与架构危机。强烈推荐给所有正在使用 LLM/Agent 操作数据库、或关注基础软件架构演进的开发者与架构师。
